clue.text: Censor Porno Dick

parts.note: blue films are pornographic
slang for penis; a pencil is a similar slender rod

explanation.surface: A demand to censor a smut-peddler called Dick.
explanation.walkthrough: Censors traditionally struck out lines with a blue pencil, so the phrase works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil a text is an idiom for cutting or suppressing its offending passages.

clue.text: Where a member joins body to provide ammunition to ex-PM outing Thatcher, initially

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons

indicators.note: the letter is put out, removed from the name

parts.note: William Pitt, Prime Minister

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Thatcher

parts.note: only its first letter is wanted, as initially says

explanation.surface: Supplying a former Prime Minister with weapons against Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the shoulder where the arm, a limb, meets the torso.

clue.text: Where to vote for Blair, say, by giving head to Cherie, professionally

definitions.text: Where to vote for Blair, say

parts.note: poll is an old word for the head, as in poll tax
Cherie Blair practised as a barrister under her maiden name, Cherie Booth

explanation.surface: Hints at a sexual favour from the Prime Minister's wife to win a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving head' looks crude, but head is simply the letters for poll.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks the ballot in a small screened cubicle at the polling station.

clue.text: Crafty thing letting off a fart, etc.

indicators.note: letting off, like an explosion, blows the letters apart into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wind-breaking novelty item.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made by human craft or skill is a handmade object, a crafted item.

clue.text: Brief shot, for instance, of heads of Arsenal mouthing more obscenities

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their first letters

parts.note: taken as written; only the first letter of each word is used

explanation.surface: Arsenal footballers swear at the ref for a brief shot of the TV cameras.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot is one example of ammunition, and the short slang form of that word is clipped, hence brief.

clue.text: Old Russian plonker holding up fool

indicators.note: the slang word holds the other inside it

parts.note: British slang for penis, as is cock

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word for fool reads bottom to top

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An old Russian idiot propping up a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were horsemen of the Tsarist Russian steppe, so one is a Russian of old.

clue.text: Nuts about chamber venues for Ted Heath once

indicators.note: the slang word for nuts goes round the outside, about the word for a chamber

parts.note: slang for testicles
a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: Mocks former Prime Minister Ted Heath by pretending his debating venues were only fit for a nutter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath here is not the Tory PM but his namesake, the big-band leader whose orchestra played dance halls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted Heath's big band toured the large public dance halls of the 1940s and 1950s, so these were its venues.

clue.text: Churchman put down — Margaret has no time for him

indicators.note: the surname has no letter for time left in it

parts.note: Margaret Beckett, Labour cabinet minister

explanation.surface: Margaret Beckett has no patience for a dismissed cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret looks like Thatcher; the cabinet minister is Beckett.
explanation.definitionFit: Archbishop Thomas Becket was killed in Canterbury Cathedral in 1170, so he was a cleric put down.

clue.text: Dicky is otherwise Cook but without the balls

indicators.note: the two letters are put otherwise, the other way round

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: the name has the round letters taken out

parts.note: Robin Cook, the Labour Foreign Secretary, taken as written
the two round O shapes in the word, like a pair of balls

explanation.surface: Robin Cook as a eunuch, otherwise known as Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for unwell or shaky, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling dicky is feeling poorly or ill, the same as being unwell.

clue.text: Action man's butt next to curvaceous Derek

parts.note: to butt is to ram with the head
Bo Derek, the actress famed for her figure in the film 10

explanation.surface: A toy soldier's backside sits beside a shapely film star.
explanation.walkthrough: Action Man is also a British boy's toy soldier, which the surface trades on.
explanation.definitionFit: John Rambo, Stallone's commando, is the archetypal hero of violent action films.

clue.text: Insinuate he's an OBN candidate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to worm one's way in, as a verb
second meaning: a toady; Private Eye awards the Order of the Brown Nose to sycophants

explanation.walkthrough: OBN is Private Eye's own joke honour, the Order of the Brown Nose, for flatterers.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip in gradually is to worm in, and a fawning sycophant is called the same word as a noun.

clue.text: Randy, wrecked by Hello! curse — long gone

indicators.note: the letters of the greeting and the curse are smashed up and rebuilt
one letter standing for long has vanished from the mix

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rebuilt
L is the abbreviation for long, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A celebrity named Randy is ruined by a jinx from appearing in Hello! magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine; its exclamation mark is part of the title, not the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Randy is British slang for sexually eager, which is what a lustful, leering person is.

clue.text: Choice oaths increasingly heard from the politician these days

definitions.text: increasingly heard from the politician these days

parts.note: an election is a choice made by voters
solemn promises

explanation.surface: Politicians are swearing more and more often lately.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared a week before the May 2005 UK general election, when such pledges filled the air.
explanation.definitionFit: During a campaign candidates pledge what they will do in office, so such pledges are what voters hear constantly.

clue.text: Nut mangling Monica dropping round about one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about the letter for one
Monica's letters are mangled into a new order
the round letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: taken as written, the name to be cut and rearranged
O is round in shape
A as the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A madman mauls Monica, perhaps Lewinsky, before falling about.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is slang for a crazy person, the same as a wild lunatic.

clue.text: Fashionable revered Royal with Sunday cricketer is right out of favour

parts.note: in fashion is in
Diana, Princess of Wales, widely revered after her death
W.G. Grace, the most famous Victorian cricketer

explanation.surface: A trendy, worshipped royal paired with a Sunday cricketer has now lost favour.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the calendar abbreviation for Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in disgrace is to have lost the approval of others, an idiom for being out of favour.

clue.text: The tosser's deposit-holding institution?

definitions.meaning: tosser is British slang for an idiot, but literally one who masturbates
reads as a bank in the financial sense, but the deposit is a donation of sperm

explanation.surface: Sounds like a sneer at a jerk's high-street bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic storing donated semen for fertility treatment is the place where such deposits are kept.

clue.text: Conservative leader, awfully patient sod in such an uncomfortable state, no shit

definitions.text: in such an uncomfortable state, no shit

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written; its leader is the first letter

indicators.note: the words are awfully jumbled into another order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Abuses a Tory leader as a long-suffering so-and-so in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke: 'no shit' both means 'really' and states the symptom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bunged up and unable to pass stools is literally in a state with no shit.

clue.text: Perhaps Hazel's cover is cobblers' nightmare

parts.note: cobblers is rhyming slang (cobbler's awls, balls) for testicles, also called nuts
a nightmare is a hell

explanation.surface: Suggests a shoemaker's worst dream is a hazel shrub's covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Hazel as one example of a nut tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard casing of a hazelnut is its shell, covering the kernel.

clue.text: Page four shameless Mowlam's a scandalous politician

indicators.note: the letters behave without shame and are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
Mo Mowlam, the Labour cabinet minister

explanation.surface: A page-four item about the outspoken Mo Mowlam being brazen.
explanation.walkthrough: John Profumo was the minister at the heart of the 1963 Christine Keeler sex scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: His affair with Keeler and lie to Parliament made him the byword for a disgraced minister.

clue.text: One very contorted bra's pressure line

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: the word bra is contorted out of shape

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A twisted bra puts strain on one's figure.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, a line joining places of equal atmospheric pressure is drawn as this.

clue.text: Tell tale marriage advisors

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to narrate or tell a story
second meaning: ..., the British couples counselling charity

explanation.walkthrough: Relate is the UK charity once called the Marriage Guidance Council.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to narrate it, and the British counselling service for couples bears the same name.

clue.text: See 12
Spare supermodel publicity spies

parts.note: Kate Moss, the famously thin model; spare means lean
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A skinny model's advertising campaign attracts the secret services.
explanation.definitionFit: Mossad is Israel's national intelligence agency, staffed by its secret agents.

clue.text: Gay, non-PC adman's praise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an offensive old slang term for a homosexual man

explanation.walkthrough: The comma separates a slur, marked as such by non-PC, from advertising copy.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflated promotional write-up is called this, and the same word was an insulting term for a homosexual.

clue.text: Exposure of member by Lily? It's most illuminating

parts.note: a flasher exposes his member; flash is the act
a lily grows from a bulb; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A streaker named Lily gives a very revealing performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera's flash lamp gives a burst of intense light, so it lights things up brilliantly.

clue.text: Royal needs date — whatever's around

indicators.note: the word for whatever goes around the date letter

parts.note: any means whatever, as in any one you like

explanation.surface: A prince needs a date, whoever turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: Andy is Prince Andrew, the Queen's second son.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew is a member of the British royal family, usually nicknamed this by the tabloids.

clue.text: Get rid of Bush!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cancel or scrap
second meaning: scrubland, low stunted vegetation

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes it a political slogan against George W. Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel a plan is to scrap it, and stunted brushwood country is the same word as a noun.

clue.text: "Exemplary" Dome's chaotic, laughable opening

indicators.note: the dome's letters are chaotic, out of order

parts.note: the Millennium Dome, taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written; its opening is the first letter

explanation.surface: The Millennium Dome was meant to be a showpiece but its launch was a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: The Millennium Dome opened on New Year's Eve 1999 to widespread ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, a model pupil or citizen is one worth copying, an ideal example.

clue.text: Such a sexy performer needs to carry own cooling equipment

definitions.meaning: a burlesque artiste who strips while hiding behind feathered props

definitions.text: needs to carry own cooling equipment
definitions.meaning: the props she holds are the kind waved to cool oneself

explanation.surface: An erotic dancer must bring her own fan to stay cool under the lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque artiste conceals herself with large ostrich-feather fans, which double as cooling devices.
